schema.title: UpdateCredentialRequest
schema.description:
Send only the fields you want to change; anything you leave out is untouched, and omitted fields
are not validated.

To change the password, use the password-rotation endpoint rather than this one.

UserName.description:
Rename the login. The old name is released and the new one must be free across the whole
service.

A name already in use returns `422`; a reserved name is rejected by validation with `400`.
Either way nothing changes. A credential that already holds a reserved name is exempt from
that check, so its other fields can still be updated.

Alias.description:
The label shown in the dashboard. Sending an empty string resets it to the login name rather
than clearing it.

Permission.description:
What this credential may do with files under its home and chroot directories. Ignored on the
organization's default credential, and on a credential that has, or is being given, virtual
folders.

HomeDirectory.description:
Where the credential lands after connecting. Sending an empty string resets it to
`/home/{UserName}`. Must start with a forward slash, must not end with one, and cannot
contain a variable such as `${...}`.

ChrootDirectory.description: The highest directory this credential can reach. Sending an empty string resets it to `/`.

HomeDirectoryDetails.description:
Replace the credential's virtual folders with this list, up to 50. The credential's
`Permission` is removed, since each folder carries its own.

Send an empty list or `null` to go back to a home directory. The credential then needs a
`Permission` again: send one in the same request, or the request is rejected with `400`
unless it already has one.

The organization's default credential cannot use virtual folders.

items.title: VirtualFolder
items.description:
One entry in a credential's virtual folders: a path the credential sees, mapped to a real
location in your storage, with its own permission.

Entry.description:
The path the credential sees, such as `/inbound`. Must start with a forward slash and must not
end with one, unless it is the root `/`, which must then be the only entry. Entries cannot
share a path or contain one another, and cannot contain a variable such as `${...}`.

Target.description:
The real location in your storage that the entry shows, as a path from the root of your
bucket. Must start with a forward slash and must not end with one. Two entries may show the
same location only if they give it the same permission.

Type.description:
Whether the entry is a folder or a single file. Defaults to `DIRECTORY`. A `FILE` entry
cannot be the root `/`.

Permission.description:
What the credential may do inside this entry. The same levels as a credential's `Permission`,
applied to this entry alone; `none` keeps the entry listed but denies everything in it.

Email.description:
Where web portal invitations and password resets are sent. Changing it clears the verified
flag until the new address is confirmed. Send an empty string to remove it.

State.description:
Whether the credential can connect. Prefer the activate and deactivate endpoints, which say
what they do at the call site.

ExpiresAt.description:
When access should stop working, in **Unix epoch seconds**, or `null` to remove the expiry.
Must be after the end of today and no more than a year away. When the time passes, the
credential becomes `inactive` and its `ExpiresAt` returns to `null`.

Settings.title: CredentialSettingsInput
Settings.description:
The settings you can change. Each part you send is merged into the current settings; within it,
a list you send replaces the stored list.

MFA.description: Multi-factor authentication for web portal sign-in.

Required.description:
Require the person using this credential to enrol and use a second factor at their
next portal sign-in.

Network.description: Where this credential may connect from.

InboundRules.description:
The credential's complete list of inbound rules, replacing the current list. Up to 250.

Takes effect only if your plan includes inbound rules. On a plan without them the list is
left unchanged and the request still succeeds, so read the credential back if it matters.

items.title: InboundRule
items.description:
One network rule that allows connections to a credential from an address or range.

A connection is accepted when **any** enabled `allow` rule matches its protocol and source
address, counting your organization's rules and the credential's own together. So a credential's
rules can only add to what the organization already allows, never restrict it. New organizations
start with one organization rule that allows every address; tighten that rule before credential
rules make a difference.

Id.description:
An identifier for the rule, unique within the credential. You choose it; the dashboard uses a
UUID.

Protocol.description:
Which connections the rule applies to: `*` for every protocol, or one of `SFTP`, `FTPS` or
`WEB_PORTAL`. Values are case-sensitive.

State.description: Whether the rule is in effect. A `disabled` rule is kept but never matches.

Action.description:
What a matching connection is allowed to do. Only `allow` rules are evaluated, so `allow` is
the only value with an effect.

Source.description:
Where the connection comes from: a single IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range such as
`203.0.113.0/24`.

Description.description: A note explaining why the rule exists. Shown in the dashboard.

homeDirectory.summary: Go back to a home directory

network.summary: Allow connections from one more range
